title: 2D Chamfer: select a minimum cone radius for the cut

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## Wanted

A 2D Chamfer can state a minimum cone radius. The cone then cuts the requested chamfer through a radial band above that radius.

This lets the user keep the selected edge and the requested chamfer width. For example, a 6 mm chamfer mill can cut a 1 mm chamfer at a 2 mm minimum cone radius. The cutting band is then 2 mm to 3 mm from the tool axis.

## Current behaviour

CamCraft places the virtual cone tip on the selected wall. It keeps the tip at:

```text
tip_z = top_z - width * tan(angle)
```

The tool centre has no XY offset from the picked line. A larger chamfer mill therefore cuts through the smallest part of its cone. The operation has no setting that moves to a larger-radius band of the same cone.

## Proposed rule

For an ideal sharp cone, add one operation value named `Minimum cone radius`.

```text
minimum cone radius = r
chamfer width = w
centreline offset toward air = r
tip_z = top_z - (r + w) * tan(chamfer angle)
contact radius = r to r + w
```

For a 45-degree chamfer, a 6 mm tool, `w = 1 mm`, and `r = 2 mm`:

```text
centreline offset = 2 mm
contact radius = 2 mm to 3 mm
tip_z = top_z - 3 mm
```

The final chamfer stays 1 mm wide. The tool uses a 2 mm to 3 mm part of the cone instead of its 0 mm to 1 mm part.

The `Side` setting determines the air side for closed rings and selected open chains.

## Safety doors

- Refuse when `r` is negative or not finite.
- Refuse when the tool radius is smaller than `r + width`.
- Refuse when the cone or flute reach cannot supply `(r + width) * tan(angle)`.
- Offset closed loops and open chains with the same air-side law.
- Refuse an offset that folds, disappears, or reaches material on the air side.
- Keep the declared `EdgeBreak` on the original picked edge with the authored width and depth. The larger contact band must not create credit for more edge work.
- Stock simulation and collision verification must judge the offset cone position, not the old tip-on-wall position.

## Scope

This issue does not model or compensate for tool-tip wear. It selects a band of the current ideal sharp cone.

Issue #895 is related because it tracks real flat, ball, and radiused tip geometry. This operation-level feature can be specified independently.

## Done means

- The Geometry page exposes `Minimum cone radius` for a 2D Chamfer.
- The value round-trips through project files and the MCP operation parameter surface.
- A 45-degree, 6 mm ideal cone cuts an authored 1 mm chamfer with a 2 mm minimum radius.
- A test proves the contact radii are 2 mm and 3 mm, and the tip path is 3 mm below the top plane.
- A motion test proves a closed ring offsets toward the side `Side` names.
- A motion test proves each selected open chain offsets toward its air side.
- The tool-radius and flute-reach refusals name the missing dimension.
- Stock simulation proves the final 1 mm edge break and no gouge on the part.
- Existing 0 mm-minimum-radius projects keep the current path byte for byte.

## Labels

Suggested triage: `enhancement`, `area:2d`, `P6`, and `effort:high`.

Changelog: A 2D Chamfer can use a selected larger-radius band of a chamfer mill while preserving the authored chamfer width.

body:
## What happens

The refusal `FirstTraverseUnderTable` (#3081) gives two heights in the local frame of the 3+2 plane. The message calls them Z values. The user sets the clearance height in the user frame, so the numbers in the message are not values that the user can type.

Generate shifts each height by `h - origin.z` into the tilted frame (`crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs`, `judge`). `table_read` returns `limit` as "a local height" (its doc comment), and `judge` puts `start_h` (also local) into `height_mm`. Nothing adds `origin.z` back before the message.

Example from `crates/app/tests/first_traverse_table.rs`, `a_head_tilt_past_90_under_the_table_is_refused_with_lower`:

- The tilt origin is at Z 20 (`ORIGIN_Z`). The user sets the clearance height to 170 (`ORIGIN_Z + 150.0`). The head tilts to B 120.
- The message says: "to the clearance plane at Z150.000 it can go under the table top - lower the clearance plane to Z113.590 or under it".
- In the user frame, the plane is at 170 and the limit is 133.590.

The verdict is correct and the post stays blocked. Only the numbers and the word "Z" in the text are wrong:

- With `origin.z` > 0, a user who types the given limit gets a plane that is lower than necessary.
- With `origin.z` < 0, a user who types the given limit gets the refusal again.
- The heights are measured along the tilted tool axis, not along machine Z, so "Z" is not correct for a tilted plane.

## Related

- #2991 fixes the same defect for `FirstTraverseLow` (PR #3080). That PR adds `in_user_frame` in `crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs` and a `tilted` text that names the raise without a Z value.
- Found when main was merged into PR #3080. Main added `FirstTraverseUnderTable` after the review of that PR.

## Possible fix

After #3080 merges: extend `in_user_frame` to `FirstTraverseUnderTable` (add `origin.z` to `height_mm` and `limit_mm`). Change the text so that it does not call a height along the tilted axis a Z value, as #2991 does for `FirstTraverseLow`. A cache field can need `#[serde(default)]`, as `tilted` has in #3080.

## Done means

- The under-table refusal on a 3+2 plane gives the plane and the limit in the frame where the user sets the clearance height.
- The text does not call a height along a tilted tool axis a Z value.
- A test pins the two numbers in the user frame (for the case above: 170 and 133.590), and the post stays blocked.

Proposed labels (a contributor cannot set labels): `bug`, `P3`, `effort:medium`, `area:multiaxis`, `area:ui`, `source:agent`. These are the labels of #2991. The defect is a misleading refusal message with a workaround, so `P3`.

body:
What happens: a 2D Pocket rest pass with a corner relief (#2400) cuts the relief at only some corners. The other corners keep their material. No note or warning tells the user.

Expected: the rest pass cuts a relief at each inside corner that the rest area touches. If it cannot cut one, it says so in a note.

Evidence:
- The pocket is 30 x 30 mm with sharp corners. The rest tool is 6 mm, with `CornerReliefKind::Dogbone`. The entered previous tool is 16 mm.
- `pocket_relief_plan` gives 4 reliefs, with the start points (3,3), (27,3), (3,27) and (27,27).
- `rest_pocket_with_relief` cuts only the relief at (3,3).
- The cause is the filter in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/rest2d.rs` (`rest_pocket_with_relief` on main): `.filter(|r| plan.center.contains(r.start))`. Each start point is on the boundary of `plan.center`. `Region::contains` gives `true` for (3,3) and `false` for the other three.
- The plain pocket (`pocket_entered_with_relief`) cuts all 4 reliefs. The rest pass where the previous tool fits nowhere also cuts all 4.

Found while I merged main into PR #2822 (#2033). The test `crates/motion/tests/rest_relief.rs` on that branch shows the result. It pins that the two rest modes agree, and does not pin the count of 4.

Workaround: use a plain pocket with the relief, not a rest pass.

Done means: a rest pass with a relief cuts each relief whose corner the rest area touches. A test pins all 4 dogbone ends on the fixture above. A relief that the pass cannot cut gives a note.

body:
## What is missing

AGENTS.md has no rule that makes an agent fix its own blocked pull requests before it starts new work. Open PRs with `conflicts` or `needs-rework` wait while agents claim new issues.

## The maintainer's words (2026-11-21)

"Lets add a new law to the AGENTS.md before each new task start. Check Pull requests that is created by current user account - that has label "conflicts, need-rework". And then fix those before picking up any new issue. Make sure this is a docs change that get pushed and merged and signaled over issue 681 as a process change. On the process change dictate that agent files and skills should be reloaded."

## Required change

- Add a new law to AGENTS.md. Name it in bold, as the other rules are named, so that skills and agents can cite it. Suggested name: **Own blocked PRs first**.
- The law: before an agent claims or starts any new issue, it lists the open PRs of the current account that carry `conflicts` or `needs-rework` (`gh pr list --state open --author @me --label conflicts` and `--label needs-rework`; the label is `needs-rework`). The agent fixes each one before it picks a new issue.
  - `conflicts`: merge `origin/main` into the branch (never rebase, never force-push), run the targeted gate, push, as the `resolve-conflicts` skill says.
  - `needs-rework`: fix each review finding on the same branch with a plain push, as "Pull Request Law" says (the PR is a draft first, `needs-rework` is replaced when the review is clean).
  - The existing orders stay first: a `P1` or `P2` PR before other PRs, and the standing order for outside PRs.
- Reconcile the existing text that this law changes. "Refresh only at merge time" says that the author's agents do not touch a conflicting PR. The new law overrides this for the PRs of the current account. Edit that bullet so the two rules do not disagree.
- Add the check as a step to the skills and agents that start work: `work-issue` (step before the claim), `.claude/agents/coordinator.md` (before it dispatches a worker for a new issue), and the `issue-worker-*` agent files if they claim an issue. Keep each edit to a few lines.
- A PR of this change has the line `Process change: yes` in its body. It does not edit `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`.

## Process change notice

The merging session runs `cargo xtask process-bump` after the merge and comments on the pinned issue #681. The comment must say: **agent files and skills must be reloaded** (a running session reloads `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/agents/` and `.claude/skills/`; a fork syncs them as `fork-sync` says). Add this "reload" line to the fixed format of the #681 comment in AGENTS.md, so that each process notice carries it.

## Done means

- The law is in AGENTS.md and the edited bullet does not disagree with it.
- `work-issue`, the coordinator agent and the issue-worker agents carry the check.
- The PR is merged, the process bump PR is merged, and #681 has the comment with the reload instruction.

body:
## What happens

A 2D Contour in `O4 Cam Plate master` still shows a linear lead-in when the user sets **Lead in/out** to **None**.

The user also sets these values:

- **Lead out > Type:** None
- **Before lead-in:** 0.0 mm
- **After lead-out:** 0.0 mm
- **Overlap past the start:** 0.0 mm

The user generates the operation again after the changes. The viewport still shows a straight line at the contour entry.

Changing the lead to **Arc** changes the entry shape. Changing it to **Linear** gives the same straight entry. Changing it back to **None** does not remove that entry.

A screenshot from 2026-11-21 shows the operation `2D Contour1`, the selected **None** values, and the remaining straight segment.

## Expected

When the lead-in and lead-out are **None**, the first XY cutting move starts on the contour path. The path has no straight or arc lead segment before that move.

Entry, plunge, retract, rapid, and level-link moves can remain. They must not appear as a lead feed at the contour seam.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a project with a closed 2D Contour operation.
2. Open **Lead in / Lead out**.
3. Set **Lead in/out** to **None**.
4. Set **Lead out > Type** to **None**.
5. Set both extensions and the overlap to 0.0 mm.
6. Click **Generate**.
7. Select the first cutting move near the contour seam.
8. Observe the remaining straight entry segment.
9. Change **Lead in/out** to **Arc**, then to **Linear**, then to **None**.
10. Observe that **Arc** and **Linear** change the shape, but **None** restores the straight entry instead of removing it.

## Related

Issue #3019 covers a generated linear lead that crosses its own ring. The report also says that `lead: "none"` posts. This issue covers a different result: the UI and the posted path still contain an entry lead when the user selects **None**.

## Done means

- A UI or app test changes a Contour from a linear lead to **None**, applies the draft, and generates the operation.
- A test asserts that the first cutting move starts on the contour path with no added lead segment.
- A test covers an explicit **Lead out > None** value with zero extensions and zero overlap.
- The generated path and posted output contain no linear or arc lead when both lead shapes are **None**.
- A regression test proves that **Arc** and **Linear** still generate their selected shapes.

Changelog: A 2D Contour with both lead shapes set to None no longer keeps a linear lead-in in the generated path (#3132).

title: Hobby router machine files start every new operation on Flood coolant, so a first post writes M8

labels.name: enhancement

body:
Reported on Discord (2026-11-21, relayed by Mike): a first-time CAM user generated G-code and found it turned on flood coolant and did a tool change, which they did not want. They did not know how to change it.

## What happens

`CoolantMode::machine_default` picks the default coolant for new operations from the machine's `coolants` list (`crates/app/tests/coolant_air.rs`, `the_machine_default_coolant_reads_the_coded_list`): Flood wins wherever it is listed. The shipped hobby machine files list Flood (M8) and Mist (M7), because the Grbl/grblHAL/TinyG controllers have those pins:

- `assets/machines/grbl-3axis.mch`
- `assets/machines/grblhal-3axis.mch`
- `assets/machines/tinyg-3axis.mch`
- `assets/machines/sienci-altmill-2x4.mch`, `-4x4.mch`, `-4x8.mch`

So every new operation on these routers starts on **Flood**, and the first post writes `M8`. Most hobby routers have no flood coolant. The M8 pin is often unwired, or wired to something else (a relay, a vacuum).

## Expected

A machine file can state the coolant that new operations start on, separately from the coolant codes it can write. The hobby router files start new operations on **Off** and still offer Flood/Mist/Air for a user who has them. Industrial mill files keep Flood.

## Notes

- This changes the coolant words in posted G-code for new operations on these machines, so the safety floor makes it `effort:high`. Existing documents keep the coolant each operation stores.
- The user guide says Flood is the default (`site/content/guide/fundamentals/chips-and-coolant.md`). Update it to say the default comes from the machine.
- Not part of this issue: the tool-change half of the report. It came from posting with the default industrial mill instead of the Grbl machine; the Grbl post already writes an M0 stop, not M6.

Done means: a machine file can declare the default coolant for new operations (a test pins that the declared default wins over "Flood wins"); the Grbl, grblHAL, TinyG and Sienci AltMill files declare Off; a new operation on those machines posts no M7/M8 (a post test); the guide page states the rule.

The user documentation has no reference for the post-processor format. A user who writes or changes a `.cps` post cannot find out what the post receives or what it must write. The user must read the source to debug a post.

A reference page in the user guide (`site/content/guide/reference/`), written in plain English. It names these items:

- The manifest properties of a post and what each one does.

body:
Found while fixing #2898.

## What happens

A flat Circular with several rings and a helix entry gets blocking `Crossing` warnings. Verification refuses the program. The post is held. The program is refused, not unsafe.

Reproduce with the job of #2898, with entry `Helix` and `helix_radius` 1:

- center [0,0], radius 10, tool EM-0600-4FL (25 mm flutes), stepover 2, stepdown 2
- top Z20, bottom Z0, clearance Z30, stock_to_leave 0

Generation reports pairs such as `feed moves 2 and 84 cross in XY at shared depth`. Each pair is a helix arc of ring k-1 and a helix arc of ring k at the same level.

## Cause

The Circular is ring-major: each ring runs its own level ladder, with its own entry at each level. Each helix passes through its ring's start, and its centre is one helix radius inward. When the stepover is two helix radii, the helix of ring k-1 touches the helix of ring k at the start of ring k. The two helices share one depth band. The crossing law (`crates/sim/src/verify/crossing.rs`) counts a touch as a crossing.

## What was tried

The fix branch of #2898 tried the pocket's z-major order for the flat mode (all rings at one plane). That removed the crossings. But the inner rings then started with an axial plunge that was not named, also under a ramp entry. Four ramp-entry tests went red. The branch dropped that approach (`docs/decisions/2898-circular-ring-links.md`).

## Expected

The helix entry of each later ring is placed so that it does not touch the helix of the ring before it, or the parameters are refused before generation with a named cause.

## Workaround

Use the plunge or the ramp entry, or one ring only.

body:
## What is missing

We want to post a CamCraft milling job as a conversational Heidenhain Klartext (`.H`) program. Our first target is a Fehlmann Picomax 55 with an iTNC 530 running NC software `340490-03`. CamCraft already writes Heidenhain DIN/ISO programs. Issue #3095 tests that post. Issue #2227 proposes a reader for Klartext files. This proposal concerns the writer.

## Proposed design

- Add one **Heidenhain Klartext** post alongside the DIN/ISO post. Keep the implementation, machine data, and test fixtures in CamCraft.
- Let the machine definition identify the installed control, its NC software, and its tool-change procedure. Record installed options when a supported feature needs them.
- Let the post select the documented syntax for that combination. For example, the Picomax needs a manual tool change with the quill at its physical change position. Other iTNC 530 machines can have a different tool changer.
- Start with one metric setup, three linear axes, stock bounds, preset selection, straight moves, plunges, and constant-height XY arcs. Refuse unsupported operations by name. Drilling cycles, tapping, probing, and tilted planes can have separate acceptance criteria later.

## What the local prototype shows

The prototype has one output implementation. It accepts the exact model and release above. Changing only the configured release to `340490-04` or `606425-04` makes it refuse the job before writing a file.

We ran two CamCraft programs on the Heidenhain iTNC 530 programming station, NC software `606425-04 SP20`. Its converter accepted all 41 blocks of a single-tool contour and all 63 blocks of a two-tool program. Test Run reached all three and five programmed stops, respectively. Both runs reached the end of the program without a logged NC error.

This supports those two programs on the station release. Acceptance on the physical `340490-03` installation remains open. Cycle 247 does not activate the preset during Test Run. Preset activation, quill clearance, and physical coolant operation still need checks on the machine. [HEIDENHAIN manuals for NC software 340 49x-03](https://content.heidenhain.de/doku/tnc_guide/html/en/index/1242135142456/1242135142480/1242135142485/1242135142485.html)

## Questions for the maintainers

1. Should the first release require an exact NC software match? When two releases document the same feature, what evidence should let them share the same output?
2. Which facts belong in the existing machine definition, and which should CamCraft maintain for each supported control? Tool-change behavior and supported cycle parameters are the first cases we would use to check that boundary.
3. Would one bounded draft PR suit the project? We propose to rework the local prototype after agreement, then submit the machine definition, post, golden output, and refusal tests together. We can split the machine-data changes first if that is easier to review. We would include the manual references, station results, and outstanding machine checks in the PR.

**Done means:** The maintainers record whether to proceed, the first supported scope, the evidence required, and the preferred PR split. We will wait for that decision before submitting code.

`fold_warnings_located` in `crates/ui/src/operations.rs` groups the warnings by a key. Two kinds on `main` use the same key:

- `Warning::AvoidHit { part: FixturePart::Shank, .. }` gives `216 + 0 = 216` (the avoid range is `216..=220`).
- `Warning::DrillUndersize { .. }` gives `216`.

A group prints only the line of its first warning. When a program has the two warnings, the pane shows one line. The second finding is not visible. The `AvoidHit` finding is a blocking verdict for a protected "Do not touch" item.

## Fix

Give `DrillUndersize` a free key (for example `223`). Add a pin in `warning_fold_tests` that folds one `DrillUndersize` and one `AvoidHit` shank hit and asserts two lines.

## Context

The clear-out refresh of PR #2836 found the defect. That refresh moved `UndercutLift` from `217` to `222` for the same reason. This issue is for the `DrillUndersize` key on `main` only.

body:
The maintainer decided on 2026-11-20: widen the verdict tolerance for a model that opens at reduced accuracy. This issue holds that work. Part of #2976.

## What happens

PR #2994 (issue #2976) opens a STEP file whose edges lie as far off their surfaces as the tolerance that the file states. The model is meshed at a coarser tolerance (up to 0.02 mm) and gets the reduced-fidelity flag and a note.

A program on that model cannot be posted. The fidelity law (#864) permits a verdict only while the excess of the mesh tolerance over the import chord is inside `DEV_TOL` (0.01 mm). The measured case: the chord is 0.02 mm, the import chord is 0.005 mm, so the excess is 0.015 mm. The law then has no verdict tolerance, and each operation is refused by name unless its stock to leave covers the excess. A finishing operation thus cannot post. The command `VouchModelFidelity` does not apply, because the chord is a measured value.

The file is legal and it opens. The user has a workaround only for roughing (stock to leave). Thus the priority is `P3`.

## What is wanted

- The verdict tolerance of such a model is the mesh deviation of the model itself, with a hard upper limit (for example 0.02 mm). The limit is a constant that no file can raise.
- The posted program says so: a comment in the program header names the model and the tolerance that the checks used. The UI shows the same fact as a note in plain English.
- The vouch command is not the mechanism for this.

## Safety

The gouge check must stay conservative in the direction that matters: the tool must not cut deeper than the real surface permits.

- The mesh can stand inside or outside the real surface by its deviation. The check must not count that deviation in favour of the tool. State the rule for each direction (a cut into the part, and material left on the part), and why a gouge of the real surface larger than the limit still blocks the post.
- The stock simulation, the keep law, the rest material and the collision checks each read the verdict tolerance. List each reader and what changes in it.
- A model at full fidelity keeps today's law, with no change of any verdict.

## Done when

- A test with a model at reduced accuracy (our own fixture, mesh deviation just under the limit) pins that a finishing operation posts, and that the program header has the note.
- A test just over the limit pins the refusal by name.
- A test pins that a real gouge deeper than the verdict tolerance still blocks the post on such a model.
- Each full-fidelity pin of the fidelity law stays green and unchanged.
- The decision file names the rule, the limit and what the user loses.

## Order

The code needs PR #2994 on `main`. The research does not.

Part of #2976. Refs #2994, #864

labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
The maintainer asked for this on 2026-11-20, after he saw that only one of the three runners works:

> The issue would need to not only split the post work into several "lanes" - it would also need to produce artifacts that gets collected and handed back for inspection. All the lanes could then be queued if we reduce the amount of runner but also run in parallell when we have more runners..

Now: `post-merge.yml` has one job, `gate`. It runs the whole batch tier (about 950 steps) on one runner. The runners `wopr` and `uma` have the label `camcraft-post-merge`. One of them works and the other waits. A run lasts about 40 minutes. The concurrency group `post-merge-main` allows one run at a time. A new push queues behind the running gate or cancels it.

Wanted:
- The batch tier is split into lanes. Each lane is one job of the workflow, for example a matrix over groups of test binaries, clippy, and the build.
- The lanes are independent. With three runners, three lanes run at the same time. With one runner, the lanes queue and give the same result as today.
- Each lane writes its logs and its result to an artifact (`gate-logs/` as `xtask gate` makes them). A final job collects all artifacts. It writes one verdict, with the red steps named, for the rolling issue `main is red (post-merge gate)`.
- A person or an agent can download the artifact of any lane and read the failure without a second run. The verdict names each lane, its runner, its time and its result.
- The report job (known defect #1611: skipped) is repaired or replaced as part of this work.

Open questions for the work:
- How `cargo xtask gate batch` splits into lanes: by a flag such as `--lane N/M`, or by named groups. The split must be deterministic, and each test binary must run in exactly one lane.
- How lanes share the build. Each runner builds the debug test binaries one time, or one job builds and uploads them. The compile cache (`sccache`) and the size of the artifacts matter here.
- How the lanes treat a push during a run (cancel all lanes, or finish and queue).
- Whether `m3` (macOS, label `camcraft-pr-test`) can join. The label rule in the `runners` skill allows a trigger only on `main` and only for self-hosted runners.

Safety (AGENTS.md "GitHub Actions minutes are budgeted"):
- No new `push`, `pull_request` or `schedule` trigger. The triggers stay as they are.
- No lane runs code of a fork PR on a self-hosted runner.
- The change touches process files (`xtask/`, the workflow, the `gate` and `runners` skills). The PR body has the line `Process change: yes`. The merging session bumps `PROCESS_VERSION` after the merge.

Done means: one push to `main` runs at least two lanes at the same time when two runners are free. The lanes together run the same test binaries as the batch tier today, with no binary lost. The collector job gives one verdict with the artifacts attached. The `runners` and `gate` skills describe the lanes.

Related: #1611 (report job skipped).

body:
## What

A Slot with a width larger than the tool diameter leaves material in its two round ends. `verify` reports no problem, and the post is not blocked.

The work on the example case `2d/slots` (#2861, part of #2392) found this.

## How to reproduce

On `main` at `ab9955105`, run this script with a model `slots` (a 100 x 60 x 12 mm block, stock of the same size):

```js
cam.call("add_tool", { catalog: "EM-0600-4FL", holder: "none" });
cam.call("add_operation", {
  kind: "Slot", name: "Slot1", tool: "EM-0600-4FL", source: "slots",
  params: {
    a: [-25.0, 15.0], b: [25.0, 15.0], width: 10.0, stock_to_leave: 0.0,
    top_z: { reference: "top_of_stock", offset: 0.0 },
    bottom_z: { reference: "top_of_stock", offset: -6.0 },
    stepdown: 3.0, stepover: 2.0, feed: 600.0, plunge_feed: 150.0, climb: true
  }
});
cam.generate();
cam.verify();   // ok
```

## What the program does

The tool is 6 mm and the slot is 10 mm wide. The tool centre must stay in a stadium of 2 mm radius around the line `a -> b`. Each level posts three rows:

```
G01 X-25. Y13. Z9. F150
G01 X25. Y13. Z9. F600
G01 X27. Y15. Z9. F600
G01 X-27. Y15. Z9. F600
G01 X-25. Y17. Z9. F600
G01 X25. Y17. Z9. F600
```

The rows touch the round end only at their end points. The tool does not follow the arc between two row ends. The move between two rows is a straight line (a chord), not an arc.

## Measured

A point check of the 10 mm stadium against the tool centre path gives these results:

- The largest leftover is 0.86 mm, on the wall of each round end at 45 degrees, where no move joins two rows.
- The leftover is 0.59 mm at the two corners where a chord joins two rows.
- The total area that is not cut is about 8.9 mm2 for each level.

The straight walls are correct. The rows at `Y13` and `Y17` cut them to size.

## Expected

One of these:

- The Slot cuts its full outline. For example, the tool follows the two half circles of the tool centre stadium at each level.
- The operation reports the leftover as a warning that names the Slot and the largest leftover.

## Workaround

- Use a smaller `stepover`. The leftover becomes smaller, but it does not go to zero.
- Use a Trochoidal slot of the same width. Its last move is a half circle around `b`, and its entry is a full circle around `a`.

## Notes

- The row law is in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slots.rs` (`SlotParams`: "each row reaches the round ends exactly as far as it can").
- The case `examples/catalog/2d/slots` shows the two programs side by side. A fix changes `slots.nc` of that case. Run `cargo xtask catalog --case 2d/slots` with the fix.

title: Turning profile offset: a steep fillet chord sends the ride far out of the bar (X354 on a 30 mm bar)

body:
Found during the work on #2394 (example case turning/cone-thread).

## What happens

A turned profile has a fillet that is tangent to a shoulder face. The first chords of the fillet are steep in (station, radius). The Profile Rough and Profile Finish rides go far out of the bar at the station of these chords, and come back. Each rung feeds through air.

Reading: a 30 mm bar, a collar of 30 mm diameter to Z20, a 1.2 mm fillet from the shoulder into a cone, insert `TN-1600-0R8`, stepdown 1.0, leave 0.25. The posted rough has, for each rung:

```
G00 X354.326 Z17.2
G01 X48.5 Z17.2 F0.0267
...
G01 X354.226 Z19.2 F0.05
G01 X353.936 Z19.209 F0.05
G01 X131.724 Z19.235 F0.05
G01 X87.392 Z19.278 F0.05
...
```

The rapid radius of the operation is also 177 mm, because it is the maximum radius of the outer rung. The finish ride of the same part goes out to X47.182.

The same model without the fillet (a sharp shoulder) posts a maximum of X48.6.

## Cause

`crates/motion/src/turning/offset.rs`, `profile_offset`, the closure `val`: a segment of slope `b` claims `a + b * (s - s0) + d * sqrt(1 + b * b)` at each station of its own window. That is the offset of the infinite line. For a steep, short segment the tangent point of the ball is not on the segment at these stations. The correct claim there is the circle about the nearer end point.

The first chord of the fillet has a slope of 16.6. With `d` = 10.05 the claim is 167 mm above the segment.

A vertical step is not affected: `segs` drops segments with equal stations.

## Effect

- The path is safe: the ride is too far out, never too deep.
- The program wastes time: about 300 mm of feed in air for each rung.
- On a lathe with a short X travel the limit gate refuses a legal program.
- The bisection toward the spike writes many very short moves (see the related issue about zero-length blocks).

## What is expected

The offset of a segment is limited to the stations where the tangent point is on the segment. Outside them the end point circles make the claim. The ride of a filleted shoulder stays within the nose radius plus the leave of the profile.

## Workaround

Model the shoulder as a sharp corner. The case of #2394 does this.

Refs #2394

labels.name: enhancement

body:
## What is asked

A contributor asks for one control on 3D Finish: a switch that turns off the waterline ring pass, so the operation cuts its raster lines only. The contributor's words, quoted unchanged (chat, 2026-11-19):

> how hard would it be to make a checkbox that can disable the waterline portion?

## What the tool does today

A Parallel 3D Finish operation splits the terrain at 45 degrees. Shallow facets get the Z-following raster lines. Steep facets get waterline rings: `parallel()` runs one raster pass, then `rings_and_tail` (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/raster.rs` line 210). The ring paths run about 90 degrees across the raster lines. Every wall that stands above the Bottom plane gets its ring ladder: hole walls, end walls, and the sloped edges of a tilted top face.

The picture below shows a contributor's test part: a long bar with a top face tilted 2 degrees and two openings, cut with a 0.3125 in ball-end, Bottom 0.300 in. The purple arrow marks one ring run that still survives on a wall near the near end. The tall ladders at the far end wall are the same law at the high end of the sloped face. The raster family cannot cover those walls; only the rings can.

![Ring run surviving on a wall at Bottom 0.300 in, parallel to the bar length and near the near end edge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/screenshots/issue-2811-waterline-arrow.png)

## Why the switch is wanted

On a part whose steep flanks are out of scope, the rings add cutting time, and they add paths the machinist did not ask for. Some machinists want the lines only, and accept the walls as they stand. One checkbox should say that choice out loud.

## Proposed shape

- One parameter, for example `waterlines: bool`, default on. Existing behaviour does not change.
- GUI name: not just "off". The control must name the consequence, for example "Steep flanks: Waterlines / Leave uncut".
- The switch applies to the Parallel pattern. Whether Parallel multi and Scallop take it is a decision. Blend should likely never take it: its 30-45 degree double cut needs the rings to remove the staircase (its own note says so). The maintainer decides this scope.

## Laws the switch must keep

1. With the switch off and steep flanks present, the path must carry a visible note that names the uncut flanks and their count. Silent rest material is not allowed (Prime Directive).
2. A model that is fully steep with the switch off must refuse with a clear error, not post an empty program. The raster answers `false` for an all-steep model; today "the rings alone carry it".
3. The parameter round-trips in the project file. Old project files load with the default, on.
4. The 3D finish MCP parameter surface exposes the same field (same rule as `fill_openings` and `gap_link`).

## Measured support (headless probe, main `744c0847b`)

Synthetic model: bar 24 x 160 mm, flat bottom z 0, top face sloped 2 degrees, two through openings, ball 7.94 mm, Parallel, gap link Jump. The probe classifies the XY direction of every Feed move.

- Bottom 0: 188 along-wall Y-family Feed runs at Z ladder levels about 0.4 mm apart. Zero Feed runs cross the open top face. All perpendicular feed sits on walls.
- Bottom raised to 9.75 mm (near the high top edge): the same perpendicular runs collapse to three ladder levels per wall, and only over the stretch where the face still stands above Bottom. Nothing sits in the open middle.

This matches the picture: raising Bottom shrank the ring set everywhere except where walls still rise above it. The behaviour is correct as designed; this issue asks for control, not for a defect fix. The probe code can become the pinning test for the switch.

## Done means

- A checkbox flips the ring pass on and off, and each state has a motion test that pins it.
- Off plus steep flanks: a note names the uncut flanks; no ring moves appear in the CL output.
- Off plus a steep-only model: a refusal with a clear message.
- Project-file round-trip test and MCP parity pass.
- The 3D finish page shows the control with its consequence wording.

## Classification

This account is a contributor and cannot set labels. Suggested labels, for a maintainer: `enhancement`, `P6`, `effort:high` (safety floor: it changes posted G-code when the switch is used), `area:motion`, `area:ui`, `area:mcp`. The body was written by the contributor's agent at the contributor's request.

body:
## What the user sees

The import of a user STEP file with a twisted B-spline flank stops with this refusal:

`a boundary point lies off the surface, outside its knot domain`

The file is legal. A different tool that reads STEP through solidcore opens the same file. The file is private and is not attached.

## Where

- The refusal comes from `Fault::Outside` in `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_nearest.rs:112`.
- The import path is the truck-stepio path.

## Cause, as found

- The surface is a degree-3 B-spline surface with a strong twist.
- The Newton search for the nearest surface point lands on a neighbouring sheet of the surface.
- The rescue grid has 4 samples for each knot span. On this surface the grid is too coarse to find the correct sheet.
- The defect is of the same class as #1602.

## Possible fixes

- Import STEP through solidcore (#917). This is the full fix.
- Or make the rescue search denser, or make it use the trim boundary.

The work decides between these and records the decision.

## Done when

- A STEP fixture that we made, with a strongly twisted degree-3 B-spline face, imports without the refusal. The fixture is not the user's file.
- A boundary point that is off the surface by more than the tolerance still gives the refusal.
- The import does not become slower by a large factor on the current fixtures.

## Effort

The importer makes geometry. Thus the safety floor applies and the effort is `effort:high`.

Requested by @vilts (relayed by the user, 2026-11-19), after the #2603 kit ran clean in his Robodrill's Manual Guide i graphic simulation: today the simulation draws a default blank, and he does not know how to set it by hand.

## What

Manual Guide i reads a blank (stock) definition block near the top of a program and uses it in the animation. An **opt-in** Fanuc post option writes the setup's stock as that block, after the program number and before the first motion.

Codes as the user's reading of the manual summarises them (to be verified against the manual):

| Code | Blank |
|---|---|
| G1902 | rectangular block: B width (X), D depth (Y), H height (Z), I/J/K = X/Y/Z distance from the block's lowest corner to the work origin |
| G1900 | round bar (along Z) |
| G1906 | round bar along X |
| G1901 / G1907 | hollow round bar (along Z / X) |
| G1903 / G1904 | square bar / hollow square bar |

Example (100 x 60 x 30 block, G54 at the top centre): `G1902 B100. D60. H30. I50. J30. K30.`

Source (public Fanuc documentation, behaviour only): Manual Guide i milling and turning operator's manual, https://www.cnc.uk.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/Manual-Guide-Milling-and-Turning-Manual.pdf

## Rules

- **Off by default.** A control without Manual Guide i can alarm on G1902, so the option is per machine (a machine/post property, e.g. "Manual Guide i blank"), never on for every Fanuc output.
- Box stock -> G1902; a cylinder stock -> G1900 (or G1906 when its axis is X); any other stock shape -> no block and a comment saying why, not a wrong block.
- I/J/K come from the setup's WCS origin relative to the stock's minimum corner, in program units (G20/G21), with the signs the manual gives. A yawed or rotated WCS that the block cannot describe -> no block plus a comment.
- No other post output changes (golden files stay the same with the option off).

## Research first (agent)

Read the manual's blank-figure section and confirm: the exact address letters and signs for G1902 and G1900 (incl. the bar's length and the axis position), where in the program the block must stand (before or after G90/G54, before the first tool change), whether it needs Manual Guide i "animation" mode only, and inch behaviour. Record the answers here before code.

## Done means

- The Fanuc post has the option, off by default; with it on, a box stock and a cylinder stock each post the right block (golden tests), and an unsupported stock posts a comment, not a block.
- vilts confirms in his Manual Guide i simulation that the drawn blank matches the stock (one short kit file).
- Clean-room: Fanuc's public manual only; no other CAM's post or output consulted.

**Research only.** No code until the open questions below are answered and the concrete sub-issues are filed (AGENTS.md "needs-research is research, not code").

## Where this comes from

A wire EDM user, Alex (@alextreseder; CamCraft Discord, 2026-11-19), asked whether our XYUV (+Z) path is collision-aware and handles swallowtails. His points, in short:

- The easy case: the wire (kerf) radius is smaller than every local radius of the part. Then each ruled face is offset with an arc join and projected onto the XY and UV planes.
- The hard case: the radius is not smaller than all local radii. Then the degenerate **local and global swallowtails** must be healed and sewn with a bounded-tolerance technique. In general this is one of the hardest CAD-kernel problems, but for wire EDM it splits into **two 2D problems** (the XY and UV planes), which makes it tractable.
- He has a working procedure (currently a FreeCAD macro) and offered to share it.

## What CamCraft does today (main)

- 4-axis ruled wire cut (#537): an upper and a lower closed profile, paired into rulings by normalised arc length or by sync points (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/ruled.rs`, `pairing.rs`); per-ruling widening (#1170, `ruled_widen.rs`).
- Kerf: each profile is offset in 2D, and the rulings are laid over those parallels.
- Degenerate results are **refused, not healed**: the fold law (the ruled surface folds back between rulings) and the crossing law (the surface crosses itself at the quarter heights) in `ruled_laws.rs`, plus the kerf and gouge laws, run before the path leaves the generator.

So the easy case works, and the hard case gives a refusal with a reason. Healing is the gap.

## Open questions

1. Which swallowtail cases occur in practice for XYUV: local (one corner tighter than the kerf radius) and global (two distant parts of a profile approach each other), on the XY plane, the UV plane, or both, and when the two planes disagree?
2. What is the healing procedure? Trim the self-intersections of each 2D offset (published offset-curve methods), then re-pair the rulings? How is the pairing kept consistent when one plane loses a loop the other plane keeps?
3. What tolerance bounds the healing, and how is the result checked (the fold and crossing laws must still pass on the healed surface)?
4. When healing changes the cut part (a corner the wire cannot reach), how is that shown to the user: the existing uncut-corner note, or a refusal when the change is above a tolerance?
5. Which of today's refusals would become healed results, and which must stay refusals (Prime Directive: correct or visibly refused)?

## What would help (from Alex or anyone)

- A **written description** of the procedure: steps, tolerances, how local vs. global swallowtails are sewn.
- If the macro itself is shared: its **licence**. We can reuse code only under a licence compatible with this project (MIT or Apache-2.0); otherwise we implement from the description and from published literature.
- **Test shapes** that make local and global swallowtails (simple STEP or DXF profiles, upper and lower). These become test fixtures for the fold and crossing laws even before any healing exists.

Clean-room: published literature, the contributor's own description, and our own design notes only; no material from Autodesk products.

## What the user wants

1. Type a text string, for example a part number `SN-0471`.
2. Pick the face to engrave and place the text on that face.
3. Set the text height and the tool.
4. CamCraft makes the engraving toolpath, verifies it and posts it.

## What exists today

- `OpType::Engrave` and `OpType::Trace` machine 2D geometry along the tool centreline. They obey the mark law (#1595): a shallow mark passes, a deep cut is refused.
- 2D geometry comes from a DXF sketch (the `Sketch` entity, #1862). Work to feed sketch chains to Engrave and Trace is #1869. SVG import is #1880.
- There is no way to make geometry by typing text. A user today must draw the letters in a CAD program, export a DXF, and import it.

## What to build

- A text-to-outline step: convert the typed string into glyph outlines as 2D regions (outer loop + hole loops for letters such as A, B, O). Use one of the fonts already bundled in `assets/ui/fonts/`; the outlines are the same vectors the UI draws. Flatten the glyph curves to polylines within the setup tolerance. Clean-room: only the font's own licensed outlines, no vendor letter shapes.
- An undoable command (for example `InsertText`): the text string, height, and the placement become a `Sketch` the operation kinds already read. Ship its MCP tool with it (#128 law).
- Placement: select a planar face (or the setup top plane) in the viewport, then set X/Y and rotation. The existing `sketch::face_frame` code gives the face frame.
- Parameters on the Engrave operation: text string, height (mm or inch through the unit lens), letter spacing, depth (bounded by the mark law), tool, feed, and climb. The toolpath path is the existing Engrave/Trace generator.
- Two ride modes later, both from the same outlines: ride the glyph boundary with a small end mill or v-bit, and single-line engraving on the glyph skeleton with a v-bit. Pick one for the first cut; record the choice in `docs/decisions/`.

## Suggested label triage

`enhancement`, `area:2d`, `P6`, `effort:high` (safety floor: new toolpath and posted G-code). The filing account has no label rights; a collaborator sets these.

> issue, p4, in the work envelope. there should be a Arrow "pointing" towards the user and the text stating "operator side".. so people understand where they look "into" the work envelope from.

## Problem

The viewport shows the work envelope of the machine. A user cannot tell from which side the operator looks into it. The user then does not know how the part sits, how the vise faces, or which way is "front".

## Wanted

1. The work envelope shows an arrow on the operator side. The arrow points toward the operator, away from the envelope. The text "Operator side" is next to the arrow.
2. The side comes from the machine. A 3-axis mill and a 4-axis or 5-axis machine have a default operator side (the front of the machine). A lathe, a router table, a laser or a plasma table can differ. The machine file may name the side. When it does not, a documented default for the machine type applies. A decision file in `docs/decisions/` records the defaults.
3. The arrow and the text follow the view: the text stays readable, the arrow stays at the envelope edge in 3D, and both do not hide the part or the toolpath. Draw them with the envelope, in the envelope colour or a muted one.
4. A switch hides them. Default: shown. The switch is a view setting (ephemeral UI state, no undo command). It sits with the other envelope display options.
5. The label text is plain English and is the same in all views. No G-code words.

## Constraints

- Layers: ui reads the machine data through the app API. A new machine-file field follows the machine-file rules and keeps old files valid (the field is optional).
- No per-frame work that can be cached (frame target under 10 ms). Build the arrow geometry once for each envelope change.
- A UI PR needs before and after screenshots in the PR body. Tests assert the presence, the text, the side for each machine type and the switch state, not pixel values. Update the layout test of the viewport page if it applies.
- Draw an original arrow. Use no asset from another product.

## Done means

- A test shows the arrow and the text for a mill, with the side as the default says.
- A test shows a machine file that names another side, and that an old file without the field still loads.
- A test shows that the switch hides and shows them.

Part of #2526 (GPU shader toolpath generation). Slice 4 of 5. Needs #2620 (compute seam).

Maintainer order (2026-11-18): "GPU shader issues get priority". Thus this issue is `P4`.

## Why
The facet gouge law measures the exact distance between each ball-center segment and each model triangle (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/gouge.rs`: `facet_gouge` lines 43-172, `dist_seg_tri` line 174). Facets are already put in XY bins (lines 65-131). On a very long program against a very large mesh the pair count is still high.

## What
- A compute kernel marks the (segment, bin) pairs whose conservative distance is below `r + margin`. f32, tile-relative coordinates, margin larger than the stated f32 error bound.
- The CPU measures every marked pair with the f64 `dist_seg_tri`. The gouge depth and its location stay the f64 values.
- The kernel only removes pairs. It never adds a gouge, and it never sets a depth.
- With no GPU, or with the GPU off, `facet_gouge` runs as today.

## Prime Directive
- A gouge must block the post. An unmarked pair that has a gouge is the one risk. Thus the filter is a superset test, and it has a CPU parity test.
- Fault injection test: a kernel margin set to a negative value must make the parity test fail. The test proves that the parity test can catch a miss.

## Pinning tests (CPU reference)
- For the gouge fixtures of the sim suites, the GPU-marked pair set is a superset of the CPU pairs with distance below `r`.
- The gouge verdicts (depth, location, refusal text) are the same with the GPU on and off.
- Skip and fail policy of `headless_gpu` (#615, `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1`).

## Decision entry
Yes, if `camcraft-sim` gets an edge onto the compute crate of #2620. Recommended instead: the app computes the pair mask and passes it to `facet_gouge` as a value, so `camcraft-sim` stays GPU-free.

Effort: `effort:max` (gouge check; safety floor).

Done means: the GPU pair filter feeds `facet_gouge`, the verdicts are equal with the GPU on and off, the superset and fault injection tests pass, and the PR states the time readings on a long program.

- Put a cylinder model in the document, rotate it with MoveModel, and take the stock "From model". This does not help every path: the simulation's field view refuses a stock that carries a rotation (see #2177).

What the work must decide:

- The controls: three axis angles (yaw, pitch, roll) on the Stock page, or an axis picker (Z / X / Y / custom).
- What the field view and the collision checks do with a tilted cylinder stock (#2177 closed one case of this refusal; a tilted primitive needs the same review).

title: sccache: crates with a build script, and solidcore below them, miss the cache in each new worktree

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
Found during the idle-box Linux measurement of #914 (https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/914#issuecomment-6991514439). Part of the #900 build cycle work.

## What happens

A fresh worktree with a warm sccache cache reaches its first app test no faster than a build without sccache. On a 12-core Linux box: 274 s with a warm cache, 264 s without sccache. The #900 goal is 3x faster.

`cargo build --timings` of a warm run (282 s wall):
- `solidcore 1.0.1` compiles for 216 s, on the critical path.
- All `camcraft-*` units together take 41 s. The first one starts at 250 s.

`solidcore` is a cache miss in each new worktree:
- The sccache hash key of `solidcore` changes with the worktree (`94ef89da...` in one worktree, `78bb5f5e...` in another). The tree and the flags are the same.
- In the same worktree, `cargo clean -p solidcore` and a rebuild gives a hit in 3 s.

The crates that miss in a new worktree are the crates with a build script, and all crates that depend on them:
- Build scripts: `serde`, `serde_core`, `thiserror`, `num_traits`, `crc32fast`, one `proc_macro2` variant.
- Dependents: `serde_json`, `flate2`, `miniz_oxide`, `rayon`, `spade`, `solidcore`, `solidcore-record`, `solidcore-ops`, `solidcore-step`, `solidcore-convert`, `solidcore-tess`.

The `.rmeta` of these crates is not the same in two worktrees (for example, `libserde-aab1de1362e9bc28.rmeta` has a different md5). This agrees with an `OUT_DIR` below each worktree's own `target/`.

`SCCACHE_BASEDIRS` (sccache 0.18.0) with the two worktree roots does not change this. `serde`, `thiserror` and `solidcore` stay misses.

## Expected

A fresh worktree with a warm cache does not compile `solidcore` again. Each worktree compiles only our own crates (the #900 intent).

## Possible directions (not tested)

- Make the build-script crates give the same inputs in each worktree, so that sccache can hit them.
- Share the compiled dependencies between worktrees in a different way. Note: AGENTS.md forbids a shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.
- Make `solidcore` cheaper in dev builds (for example, its `opt-level`), and measure the effect on the suites that use it.

## Environment

Linux (Manjaro), 12 cores, 32 GB RAM, rustc 1.98.0, sccache 0.18.0, `upstream/main` `c605e5687`. At `7cab31eea`, the dev profile, the `solidcore` pin and the sccache code in `xtask/src/exec.rs` are the same.

## Labels

I cannot set labels (no triage access). Suggested: `P7`, `effort:medium`, `area:build`. Filed by an agent session for a contributor, thus `source:agent` also applies.

Done means: a fresh worktree with a warm sccache cache gets a cache hit for `solidcore`, and the time to the first app test is measured and posted against the #914 numbers.

## Request

A built-in post for Hurco mills with the WinMax control, writing **NC/ISO programs** (Hurco's ISNC dialect, the Fanuc-like one), plus a machine file for a typical 3-axis Hurco VMC. Conversational (Hurco's own format) is out of scope.

A machine owner in the community runs a Hurco with **WinMax 09.01.393.30 (May 2019)**, NC/ISO programs only. WinMax simulates the full toolpath on the machine's screen, so each program can be checked at the control before it cuts, like the PathPilot Hub checks for Tormach.

## Clean-room sources (only these)

- Hurco's public WinMax help: the NC programming G-code table (it marks which codes are ISNC, BNC or both), NC M codes, NC part programming principles, NC parameters (support.hurco.com, WinMax Mill help, NC_Programming section).
- Hurco's public WinMax Mill documentation PDF (704-0116-101).
- What the owner's WinMax simulator accepts and shows.
- Never another CAM product's Hurco post or its output.

## What to decide from the docs

- Program start and end words, program number/comment format, units (G20/G21), the safe start line.
- Tool change (`T.. M6`) and length offset (`G43 H..`); does WinMax want a separate tool-length table call.
- Canned cycles available in ISNC (G73, G81-G89 with G98/G99) and their word formats (Q, P dwell units).
- Arcs (I/J/K vs R), work offsets (G54-G59 and the extended set), coolant, spindle words.
- Anything ISNC requires that Fanuc does not, or refuses that Fanuc allows.

## Done means

- A built-in post `Hurco WinMax (NC)` and a machine file.
- Goldens for contour, pocket, drill, peck, tap, two tools, two work offsets; a test that no word outside the documented ISNC set is written.
- One short program per question checked in the owner's WinMax simulator (load without error, the sim path matches CamCraft's), recorded on this issue.

Turning (profile, groove, thread, face, part-off), 2D (face, pocket, contour, adaptive, drill pattern, chamfer/deburr), 3D (adaptive roughing, parallel/waterline finish, rest), multi-axis (3+1 indexed - after #2389, wrapped A, 3+2), wire/sinker EDM, plasma/laser, probing.

title: Tool body: a holder band that only touches the shank top widens the judged shank

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Found during #2176 (PR #2179).

## What happens

`HolderProfile::enclose` (`crates/tools/src/holder_profile.rs`) sets the judged `shank_d` from `reach_over(flute_len, shank_top)`. `reach_over` uses inclusive bounds (`b.above <= hi && b.above + b.len >= lo`). Thus a holder band that starts exactly at the shank top widens the full judged shank to the band radius.

Example: the catalog tool `EM-0400-2FL` (Ø12 shank) with a drawn cone holder from r 10 to r 30 at the shank top. The judged `shank_d` is 60 mm. The shank laws then sweep a Ø60 shank from the flute top to the holder foot.

## Why it matters

The result is conservative, so it is not a gouge. But it can refuse a legal program: a shank law can report a collision that the real Ø12 shank does not make.

## Open questions

- Must the bound be exclusive at the shank top, or must only the band part below the shank top count?
- Which tests pin the current widening on purpose (#368, #828)?

Done means: a test pins that a band that only touches the shank top does not widen the judged shank, and no collision law reads a smaller body than the real one.

This is under the safety floor (a collision check), so it is `effort:high`.

body:
The depth ladder of the depth-stepping operations keeps the remainder in the last step. Some users expect equal steps.

What happens:

- The shared level law `camcraft_motion::machining2d::cut_levels` steps down by the full stepdown from Top Z.
- The last level ends at Bottom Z exactly. The last step is the remainder.
- Example: Top Z 20, Bottom Z 2, stepdown 5 gives the levels `[15, 10, 5, 2]`. The last step is 3 mm. The other steps are 5 mm.

The other choice:

- Equal steps: the same number of levels, `ceil(span / stepdown)`, and each step is `span / count`.
- The same example gives four steps of 4.5 mm: `[15.5, 11, 6.5, 2]`.
- Each step stays at or below the stepdown. The load on the tool is more equal, and the last pass is not a light rub.

Where it came from: found while fixing #2004 (the ladder now starts one stepdown under Top Z). The fix kept the remainder and recorded this choice in `docs/decisions/2004-top-z-level.md`, decision 7.

Notes:

- This changes posted G-code of each depth-stepping operation (safety floor: `effort:high`).
- By the project rule "CAM choices are parameters", equal steps is an operation parameter with a default, not a silent change of the law.
- The callers are listed in the audit table of the PR for #2004.

Done means:

- A decision says which ladder is the default, and if the other is a parameter.
- If a parameter is added: it is on each depth-stepping operation, it is undoable through `EditOperationParams`, it has an MCP field, and a test pins the levels of the two modes.

body:
> bug; tools like plasma cutter - or laser for that matter, and prob waterjet as well. Would require piercing and dwell data.. Lasers usually have 1-4 piercing steps that can be used all or just one. just to get thru different thickness of material. Same with plasma.. piercing height, power at height, pressure of gas, movement of torch/laser head etc etc. Use perplexit to research this in a subagent and make a issue ticket from it where this types of tools getter better coverage.

(Maintainer, 2026-11-13, in chat.)

## What exists today

- Plasma only. `ToolKind::Torch` (`crates/tools/src/tools.rs`) is a kerf width plus rpm 0; it carries no cutting data. I found no laser or waterjet tool kind in `tools.rs`.
- The plasma operation (`crates/motion/src/plasma/mod.rs`, `emit.rs`; app side `crates/app/src/operation/types/plasma.rs`, `crates/app/src/project/plasma_dto.rs`; page `crates/ui/src/egui_app/plasma_page.rs`) has three optional per-operation numbers: pierce height, cut height, pierce delay. Left empty means "set by the controller" (AutoFS).
- The Tormach plasma post (`assets/posts/tormach-plasma.cps`) writes M207/M208/M209 for those three values and G16 for the pierce, and leaves volts, amps and gas to the control's own table. Nothing else (power, gas, pressure, torch motion at the pierce) can be stated anywhere.
- Related open issues: 621 (plasma research umbrella), 1447 (common-line cutting and marking), 1452 (DXF import for 2D cuts). No open issue covers pierce data; a "pierce" search finds only closed plasma work (670, 671).

## What is missing

1. Cut data lives on the operation, not on the tool, and is not keyed by material or thickness. Changing plate thickness means re-typing numbers.
2. Only one pierce, with one height and one delay. No transfer height, no puddle-jump (lift after pierce), no creep or start-speed ramp on exit, no amperage or gas on the tool.
3. Laser and waterjet have no tool kind, so there is nowhere to put multi-stage pierce data.
4. Posts have no way to say "this stage cannot be written in this dialect".

## Research summary (facts and concepts only, own words)

Plasma
- Transfer height: the low height where the arc first transfers to the plate. Pierce height: the higher height held while the arc pierces (limits spray onto the torch). Pierce delay: time held after transfer before the head moves. Cut height: stand-off while cutting. Torch height control holds a target arc voltage as a stand-in for the distance during the cut.
- Puddle jump (optional): after the pierce, lift to a percentage of pierce height for a short dwell to clear molten metal, then drop to cut height.
- Each system and consumable set has a maximum pierce thickness; thicker plate needs an edge start (the arc begins off the plate edge). Kerf comes from the cut chart.
- The maker's cut chart is the source of values (current, gas type and pressure, heights, voltage, speed). It normally sits in the control's material table; the program selects it and may override single values.

Laser
- Makers document up to four sequential pierce stages, each with its own time, power, pulse frequency, duty cycle, focus, nozzle distance, gas type and pressure; a stage with zero time is skipped. Parameters may ramp from a start to an end value inside a stage.
- Pierce kinds named by makers: ramped, pulsed (gradual), and a forceful short pierce; definitions vary by machine, so the data model must not hard-code them.
- Cooling dwell or gas blow is machine-specific; no standard length exists.
- Normal practice: the technology table (material and thickness) holds the recipe, the NC program selects the table and pierce type and may override.

Waterjet
- Methods: stationary, dynamic (moving toward the path while piercing), wiggle or circular (short oscillation), and low-pressure or pressure-ramp pierce for brittle or laminated material (glass, stone, ceramic, composites). Abrasive can be delayed after water starts, or fed first with pressure ramped up from low.
- No universal pierce time by thickness exists; it depends on material, pressure, nozzle and method, so it must be the user's value.

Control table versus program: recipes are usually in the control's table (selected by material and thickness) with the program choosing and sometimes overriding. A CAM system therefore needs both: store the recipe, then either post the selector or post explicit values, by dialect.

## Proposed data model

A cut-data record per tool, keyed by material and thickness (rows the user adds, copies and deletes):

- Cut parameters: cut height, feed, kerf; for plasma amperage, gas type and pressure, arc voltage; for laser power, frequency, duty, gas type and pressure, nozzle distance, focus; for waterjet pressure and abrasive flow.
- Pierce: an ordered list of 0 to 4 stages, every stage optional and individually enableable. Each stage has height, duration (dwell), power or pressure, frequency and duty (laser), gas and pressure, an optional ramp end value, and head motion during the pierce (none, wiggle or circular amplitude, or moving toward the path). Plasma uses one stage plus optional transfer height and puddle-jump (percent and dwell). Waterjet adds method, low-pressure value and abrasive delay.
- Pierce capacity per record: maximum pierceable thickness, and whether an edge start is allowed.
- Every number is entered by the user or copied from the maker's chart. Shipped example rows are marked "example" in the file and in the UI.

Editing: a cut-data table on the tool page (undoable commands, an MCP tool and script verb per the command law). The operation chooses a row (or "none: the machine's own table") and may override single values; overrides are commands too.

Operation behaviour: pierce at the start of the lead-in, run the stages in order (height move, dwell and head motion per stage), then the cut-height move and lead-in. The generated path carries the stages as records in the CL file so the post and the verifier read the same data.

Posts: each dialect writes the stages it can (dwell, height moves, selector codes or direct values). A stage or value the dialect cannot express makes the post refuse with a named reason, or write a visible comment line naming what was left to the control; it is never dropped silently. The Tormach post keeps M207/M208/M209 for the plasma values and refuses a multi-stage laser record.

## Safety rules

- A thickness above the tool's pierce capacity is refused, unless the operation states an edge start (then the lead-in must start off the plate, and that is verified).
- No silent default for a pierce time or height: an empty value either posts "controller's table" as an explicit, commented choice on a dialect that has one, or refuses.
- Stage values are checked at command creation (non-negative times and heights, power within 0 to 100 percent, at most four stages).
- Values are the user's and the machine maker's; shipped examples are labelled as examples and nothing was run on a real machine. Verification (stage order, pierce inside a kept part, head motion hitting a neighbour) joins the existing plasma laws.
- This changes posted output, so it is at least effort:high.

## Suggested slices

1. Tool-side cut-data record for the existing plasma torch (material and thickness rows, transfer height, puddle jump, pierce capacity), project file round-trip, undoable commands, MCP tool. The operation picks a row.
2. Plasma generation and the Tormach post use the row; refusal for thickness above capacity and the edge-start rule; laws and goldens.
3. Laser tool kind and machine kind with 1 to 4 pierce stages; CL records and a first laser post (dwell and height moves, explicit comment lines).
4. Waterjet tool kind: pierce methods, low-pressure pierce, abrasive delay; post support.
5. Docs and shipped example rows.

Slices 3 and 4 may need their own research issues for machine kinds; file them when slice 1 lands.

Done means: a plasma, laser or waterjet tool carries material and thickness keyed cut data with up to four ordered optional pierce stages; the operation uses the chosen row at the lead-in start; each post writes every stage or refuses or comments what it cannot; a too-thick plate without an edge start is refused; tests pin all of these.

Related: 621, 1447, 1452, 670, 671.

What is missing: there is no V-carve operation. The engrave ride follows a line at one depth; it does not set depth from the width of the region.

Wanted: a 2D operation "V-carve" for V-bits (included angle from the tool). For closed regions (text, signs, inlays) the tool centre follows the medial axis and the depth at each point is the one where the cone touches both walls, limited by a maximum depth. Where the region is wider than the cone reaches at maximum depth, an optional flat-clearing pass (same or a second flat tool) removes the floor. Parameters are user choices with defaults: max depth, flat clearing on/off and its tool, start depth, stepdown for deep carves.

Safety: the cone must never cut outside the selected region at any depth (pinned by a test that sweeps the cone along the path against the region outline). A tool that is not a V-bit, an open region, or a tip flat larger than the narrowest feature is refused by name. Undoable command, MCP tool, simulation and collision checks like any 2D op.

Sources: step one of the work is a literature search (Perplexity) for published papers and handbooks on medial-axis / Voronoi-based V-carving; the algorithm is written from those and named in the module provenance comment. camlib is a feature list only: no code is copied or adapted from it.

body:
Found while working #984.

**What happens:** the same commit plans the same part differently on two platforms. `app pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` (release) on ecb54b7f:

| platform | rings levels | moves / planar / arcs |
|---|---|---|
| Windows (the #850 measure, PR #865) | Z 20.000 | 5530 / 5497 / 600 |
| macOS, Apple silicon (Homebrew rustc 1.99.1) | Z 20.000 (crossing at -2.33, -2.78) | 5786 / 5753 / 651 |

macOS is deterministic run to run, so it is not hash-map order. Rust does not contract `a*b+c` into FMA unless asked, so the most likely cause is the platform libm: `f64::sin`, `cos`, `atan2`, `hypot`, `exp`, `powf` call the system math library (MSVC CRT, glibc, Apple libm), which are not correctly rounded and differ in the last place. The STEP tessellation and the adaptive planner both use them, and the planner's crossing and acceptance tests are knife edges a 16 nm change flips (#882, #982). Not yet confirmed which call sites diverge, and not run on Linux.

**Why it matters:** a toolpath (and so the posted G-code) for the same part, tool and parameters depends on the OS the user runs. Every output is still verified and a crossing plan is refused by name, so this is not a gouge; but golden counts and exact plan pins cannot hold across platforms, and a user can see a different path from the same project file on two machines.

**Possible directions (open):** route the geometry and planner transcendental calls through a pure-Rust deterministic libm (the `libm` crate is already in Cargo.lock) so every platform rounds the same; or make the planner's decisions robust to sub-micron perturbation (#882, #982). Either changes toolpaths and needs every adaptive fixture re-measured.

Done means: the cause is confirmed on a second platform (Windows or Linux run of the bore test, plus which calls diverge), and either the output is made platform-identical with goldens re-measured, or the decision not to is recorded.

Refs #984, #882, #982.

body:
Found by the STEP bench of #916 (`crates/kernel/tests/step_agreement.rs`), at the solidcore pin `55d0e7638b9e1ebbf91ab8c10657e595c114ecda`.

**1. Wrong bounding box (the one that matters).**
`testdata/models/Milling-test.step` (and its inch twin) is a 60 mm disc with a flat at Y = 19.719. Imported through `camcraft_kernel::solidcore_step`, the solid's volume (52808.744 mm^3) and area (11143.378 mm^2) agree with truck's mesh to 1.2e-4, but `StepSolid::measure`'s box - the port's `calculate_bounding_box` with `tight: true` - is `[-30, -30, -5]..[30, 30, 20]`. The file's own vertices, truck's mesh and solidcore's own mesh (`solidcore-tess`) all stop at Y = 19.719. The box takes the whole R = 30 cylinder, not the trimmed face. It is pinned in the bench as `disagree: bounding box`.

Not known yet: whether the port's box is wrong for any trimmed periodic face, or whether the record-to-kernel build (`solidcore_convert::brep::to_kernel_body`) gives the face a parameter box that covers the whole circle. A kernel-made fixture (a cylinder cut by a plane through the seam's own booleans) would tell the two apart.

Why P1: stage 5 (#917) puts imported geometry under every toolpath. A box 10 mm too large would mis-size automatic stock and mis-place anything aligned to the part's extent.

**2. Stale cached topology after the build.** `to_kernel_body` hands out a B-rep whose cached `Face::shell` is behind its face-use links on every fixture; the port's `topology::integrity::check` refuses it ("cached face shell: face 0 not found"). The seam works around it with `Brep::refresh_cached_topology()` (public; rewrites the cached fields only). To report upstream (tangency-labs/solidcore); the maintainer decides who files it there.

**3. No cancellation in the STEP topology pass.** `solidcore_step::topology::read_solids` takes no progress or cancel hook, so the importer's time bound cannot stop it; it is bounded only by the reader's caps and the seam's 64 MiB size bound. To raise upstream, or to bound by calling the per-solid readers from the seam.

Part of #27. Gates #917.

Done means: the Milling-test rows of the bench read `agree` (the box fixed at its source, or the importer taking its box from a source that is right, with the reason recorded), the root cause is named in a decision entry, and findings 2 and 3 are either fixed at a new pin or filed upstream with their links here.

title: One machining-frame seam: OpFrame composes part_alignment and TiltedFrame

labels.name: area:multiaxis
